key_insight: ARISE uses authentic-content geometry as a stable reference to learn emerging multimodal forgeries while reducing forgetting of earlier attacks.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets continually updated multimedia verification systems, not solid mechanics or constitutive modeling.
method: Fit a real-only Gaussian mixture model to projected authentic replay representations.
Use GRASP to constrain historically stable representation directions while preserving plasticity elsewhere.
Use VAR to emphasize vulnerable replay stages based on density degradation, boundary confusion, and authentic-mode drift.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved historical retention and final average performance over representative continual-learning baselines across three Fable-Bench attack-evolution protocols and multiple detector architectures, without numerical results.
watch_item: Implementation requires replay data and reliable authentic-density estimates; inference uses only the original backbone and binary classification head.
paper_title: ARISE: Authentic Reference-Informed Stability Enhancement for Continual Multimodal Forgery Detection
